newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips slip, techs hold some gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips slip, techs hold some gains.

text.p: The Dow industrials slid to negative ground on Tuesday morning, following the long bond lower, while the technology sector managed to hang on to meager gains.
The Dow Jones Industrial average shed around 35 points, or 0.45 percent, to 7888. It moved lower as the long bond, which had been relatively flat, lost 7/32 to 6.57 percent.
The Nasdaq composite remained positive, adding around five points, or 0.35 percent, to 1529.
Equities markets were focused on a steady stream of second quarter earnings results, analysts said.

"Each company seems to dancing to its own earnings-reporting tune," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp. "Some are dancing to a waltz and others to a funeral dirge...The volatility game continues."
Texas Instruments Inc stock jumped 8-7/16 to 105-15/16, after reporting second quarter earnings of $1.07 per share compared with $0.21 per share last year.
